name: hub
summary: One always-on devbox manages the others: it lends short-lived boxes, signs in to your MCP servers once, and watches every devbox's disk.
day: An agent borrows a fresh box for a big job and gives it back when it is done. Every machine reaches your MCP servers through the hub, and a devbox that fills its disk is cleaned before you notice.
cost: One devbox that stays on, a Coder deployment for the boxes, and some setup on that devbox. Every other machine keeps working when the hub is down.
risk: The hub holds sign-ins for your MCP servers and can start, stop, and delete your boxes. Keep it as private as your laptop.

settings.question: What is the SSH name of your hub, the always-on devbox that manages the others, such as my-hub?
What is the address of your Coder deployment, such as https://coder.example.com?
Which Coder template do new boxes start from?
How many gigabytes of disk does a new box get?
How many stopped boxes may the pool keep warm for the next job?
After how many hours without a running thread is a box idle, so the hub stops it?
After how many days stopped is a box given back to the pool or deleted?
Which folders in ~/dev should a reused box keep, separated by spaces? Every other folder there is removed before the next job.
Which command warms a pooled box each night, such as a dependency install in your main checkout? Leave it empty to skip.
Below how many free gigabytes does the hub clean a devbox's disk?
Below how many free gigabytes after a cleanup does the hub tell you?
What is your Slack member ID, so only your own messages start threads? In Slack, open your profile, then More, then Copy member ID. Leave it empty to use the one the PostHog pack has.
Which emoji on your Slack message starts a thread, without the colons?
Which private host name do your devboxes use to reach the hub over HTTPS, such as hub.internal.example.com? Leave it empty to reach it over SSH tunnels only.
Which port on the hub do the SSH tunnels from your devboxes use?

workflows.name: Boxes
workflows.sentence: An agent borrows a short-lived devbox from a warm pool for a big job, links it to T3 Code, and gives it back when the job ends.

moment.title: A fresh box in a minute
moment.body: A thread needs a clean machine for a long test run. It borrows a warm box from the pool, runs there, and returns the box when it is done.

workflows.name: MCP gateway
workflows.sentence: The hub signs in to your MCP servers once, and agents on every machine reach them through it.

moment.title: Every tool, signed in once
moment.body: An agent on your laptop reads a Slack thread and an agent on a fresh box queries your analytics, both through the hub. You signed in to each tool once.

workflows.name: Disk watch
workflows.sentence: The hub cleans a devbox whose disk runs low, and tells you only when the cleanup cannot free enough.

moment.title: A full disk you never saw
moment.body: A devbox dropped under its free-space floor after a big build. The hub cleaned old caches and worktrees on it, so your threads kept running.

workflows.name: Hub links
workflows.sentence: The hub keeps SSH tunnels and T3 links to every devbox open, so each one can start threads on the others.

moment.title: Every devbox reaches every other
moment.body: A thread on one devbox hands a task to another. The hub keeps the tunnels and links between them renewed every night.

workflows.name: Slack trigger
workflows.sentence: An emoji on your Slack message, or your reaction to someone else's, starts a T3 thread about it.

moment.title: A thread from a Slack emoji
moment.body: A teammate reports a bug in Slack. You react with one emoji, and a thread starts on a devbox to find the cause.

workflows.risk: Your Slack messages and the threads they belong to become agent prompts. Only your own messages and reactions start a thread.

checks.say: This machine cannot reach the MCP gateway. Run fleet mcphub check here to see why; on the hub, fleet mcphub grant <this machine's SSH name> gives it a key.
